newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua ruling on election appeal due by Friday.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua ruling on election appeal due by Friday.

text.p: After more than a month of post-electoral squabbling, Nicargua will announce the official winners of the country's October 20 general elections on "Friday at the latest," a top election official said on Wednesday.

Nicaragua's Supreme Election Council (CSE) was due to rule Wednesday on the Sandinista Front's appeal of the original election results, but it has delayed the announcement to Thursday or Friday, CSE officials said.
The initial tally gave 51 percent of the vote to conservative Arnoldo Aleman of the Liberal Alliance, compared with 37.7 percent for Daniel Ortega, the left-wing Sandinista candidate.
But Ortega refused to concede defeat, and the Sandinistas appealed the vote as fraudulent, demanding new elections be held in the populous provinces of Matagalpa and Managua.
CSE official Ana Maria Gutierrez told reporters on Wednesday that revised results would not vary much from the figures already released.
"The revisions were done because it was the CSE's duty to do them, and the political parties right to demand them, but the final results are not going to vary much," Gutierrez said.
Ortega has warned the post-election crisis would "deepen" if the CSE upholds the status quo. He said he would recognize the "legality" but not the "legitimacy" of a future Aleman government.
The elections had been disorderly. Results from more than 200 of the 8,995 voting stations were lost, and delays in the vote count led to political uncertainty.
International observers have judged the elections flawed but fair and discounted allegations of widespread fraud.
